segments.text: Hello my friends.
segments.ipa: /həˈloʊ maɪ frɛndz/

segments.text: Welcome back to English Unleashed. I'm Tom.
segments.ipa: /ˈwɛlkəm bæk tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ənˈliʃt aɪm tɑm/

segments.text: In today's episode, I'm going to talk about a very useful book called The Practicing Mind.
segments.ipa: /ɪn təˈdeɪz ˈɛpəˌsoʊd aɪm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tu tɔk əˈbaʊt ə ˈvɛri ˈjusfəl bʊk kɔld ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd/

segments.text: The author is Thomas Sterner.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɔθər ɪz ˈtɑməs ˈstɝnər/

segments.text: This book is about practice.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs bʊk ɪz əˈbaʊt ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: It is about patience.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz əˈbaʊt ˈpeɪʃəns/

segments.text: It is about focus.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz əˈbaʊt ˈfoʊkəs/

segments.text: It is about how to stay calm while you are trying to improve at something.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz əˈbaʊt haʊ tu steɪ kɑm waɪl ju ɑr ˈtraɪɪŋ tu ˌɪmˈpruv æt ˈsʌmθɪŋ/

segments.text: It is a very helpful book for anyone learning a skill.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ə ˈvɛri ˈhɛlpfəl bʊk fɔr ˈɛniˌwʌn ˈlɝnɪŋ ə skɪl/

segments.text: Maybe you are learning English.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Maybe you are learning music.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈmjuzɪk/

segments.text: Maybe you are learning how to write, speak, teach, work, or build a better life.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ haʊ tu raɪt spik titʃ wɝk ɔr bɪld ə ˈbɛtər laɪf/

segments.text: The message of this book can help you.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈmɛsədʒ ʌv ðɪs bʊk kæn hɛlp ju/

segments.text: The main idea is very simple.
segments.ipa: /ðə meɪn aɪˈdiə ɪz ˈvɛri ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: Enjoy the process.
segments.ipa: /ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: The process means the steps you take every day.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs minz ðə stɛps ju teɪk ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: It means the practice.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ðə ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: It means the small actions.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ðə smɔl ˈækʃənz/

segments.text: It means the daily work.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ðə ˈdeɪli wɝk/

segments.text: The result is the thing you want at the end.
segments.ipa: /ðə rɪˈzʌlt ɪz ðə θɪŋ ju wɑnt æt ðə ɛnd/

segments.text: For example, speaking English fluently is a result.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈspikɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluəntli ɪz ə rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: Playing a difficult song beautifully is a result.
segments.ipa: /ˈpleɪɪŋ ə ˈdɪfəkəlt sɔŋ ˈbjutəfli ɪz ə rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: Writing a book is a result.
segments.ipa: /ˈraɪtɪŋ ə bʊk ɪz ə rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: Building a successful business is a result.
segments.ipa: /ˈbɪldɪŋ ə səkˈsɛsfəl ˈbɪznəs ɪz ə rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: But the process is what you do today.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz wʌt ju du təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Listening for 10 minutes is process.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsənɪŋ fɔr ˈmɪnəts ɪz ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Repeating one sentence is process.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈpitɪŋ wʌn ˈsɛntəns ɪz ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Writing one paragraph is process.
segments.ipa: /ˈraɪtɪŋ wʌn ˈpærəˌɡræf ɪz ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Taking one smallest step is process.
segments.ipa: /ˈteɪkɪŋ wʌn ˈsmɔləst stɛp ɪz ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: The author says that many people become unhappy because they focus too much on the result.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɔθər sɛz ðæt ˈmɛni ˈpipəl bɪˈkʌm ənˈhæpi bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ ˈfoʊkəs tu mʌtʃ ɑn ðə rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: They think about where they want to be and then they compare it with where they are now.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk əˈbaʊt wɛr ðeɪ wɑnt tu bi ənd ðɛn ðeɪ kəmˈpɛr ɪt wɪð wɛr ðeɪ ɑr naʊ/

segments.text: This creates stress.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs kriˈeɪts strɛs/

segments.text: They say, "I'm not good enough yet.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪm nɑt ɡʊd ɪˈnʌf jɛt/

segments.text: I am too slow.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm tu sloʊ/

segments.text: I should be better.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ʃʊd bi ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: Why am I still making mistakes?
segments.ipa: /waɪ æm aɪ stɪl ˈmeɪkɪŋ mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Why is this taking so long?"
segments.ipa: /waɪ ɪz ðɪs ˈteɪkɪŋ soʊ lɔŋ/

segments.text: This way of thinking makes practice painful.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs weɪ ʌv ˈθɪŋkɪŋ meɪks ˈpræktəs ˈpeɪnfəl/

segments.text: If you always look at the result, the present moment feels like a problem.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈɔlˌweɪz lʊk æt ðə rɪˈzʌlt ðə ˈprɛzənt ˈmoʊmənt filz laɪk ə ˈprɑbləm/

segments.text: You feel that today is not enough.
segments.ipa: /ju fil ðæt təˈdeɪ ɪz nɑt ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: You feel that your current level is not enough.
segments.ipa: /ju fil ðæt jɔr ˈkɝənt ˈlɛvəl ɪz nɑt ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: You feel that practice is only something you must suffer through before you get the reward.
segments.ipa: /ju fil ðæt ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈoʊnli ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju mʌst ˈsʌfər θru bɪˈfɔr ju ɡɛt ðə rɪˈwɔrd/

segments.text: But this book teaches a different way.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðɪs bʊk ˈtitʃəz ə ˈdɪfərənt weɪ/

segments.text: Practice is not punishment.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz nɑt ˈpʌnɪʃmənt/

segments.text: Practice is not a boring road before life begins.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz nɑt ə ˈbɔrɪŋ roʊd bɪˈfɔr laɪf bɪˈɡɪnz/

segments.text: Practice is life.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz laɪf/

segments.text: Practice is where growth happens.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz wɛr ɡroʊθ ˈhæpənz/

segments.text: Practice is where your mind becomes stronger.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz wɛr jɔr maɪnd bɪˈkʌmz ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: Practice is where your skill becomes deeper.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz wɛr jɔr skɪl bɪˈkʌmz ˈdipər/

segments.text: This is very important for English learners.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz/

segments.text: Many learners say, "I will be happy when I am fluent."
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz seɪ aɪ wɪl bi ˈhæpi wɛn aɪ æm ˈfluənt/

segments.text: But what happens before fluency?
segments.ipa: /bʌt wʌt ˈhæpənz bɪˈfɔr ˈfluənsi/

segments.text: If you only wait for fluency, you may feel unhappy for many years.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈoʊnli weɪt fɔr ˈfluənsi ju meɪ fil ənˈhæpi fɔr ˈmɛni jɪrz/

segments.text: Every mistake feels sad.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri mɪˈsteɪk filz sæd/

segments.text: Every slow conversation feels bad.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri sloʊ ˌkɑnvərˈseɪʃən filz bæd/

segments.text: Every difficult listening exercise feels terrible.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛvəri ˈdɪfəkəlt ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈɛksərˌsaɪz filz ˈtɛrəbəl/

segments.text: You keep thinking, "I'm not there yet."
segments.ipa: /ju kip ˈθɪŋkɪŋ aɪm nɑt ðɛr jɛt/

segments.text: But what if you change the focus?
segments.ipa: /bʌt wʌt ɪf ju tʃeɪndʒ ðə ˈfoʊkəs/

segments.text: What if you say, "Today I am practicing.
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf ju seɪ təˈdeɪ aɪ æm ˈpræktəsɪŋ/

segments.text: That is enough."
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: What if you say, "This sentence is my work today."
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf ju seɪ ðɪs ˈsɛntəns ɪz maɪ wɝk təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: What if you say, "This mistake is not a failure.
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf ju seɪ ðɪs mɪˈsteɪk ɪz nɑt ə ˈfeɪljər/

segments.text: It is part of practice."
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz pɑrt ʌv ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: What if you say, "I do not need to arrive today.
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf ju seɪ aɪ du nɑt nid tu ərˈaɪv təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: I only need to practice today."
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈoʊnli nid tu ˈpræktəs təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: This makes learning lighter.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs meɪks ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈlaɪtər/

segments.text: It makes practice calmer.
segments.ipa: /ɪt meɪks ˈpræktəs ˈkɑmər/

segments.text: The book says that when we focus on the process, we become more patient.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk sɛz ðæt wɛn wi ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs wi bɪˈkʌm mɔr ˈpeɪʃənt/

segments.text: We stop fighting the present moment.
segments.ipa: /wi stɑp ˈfaɪtɪŋ ðə ˈprɛzənt ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: We stop thinking that practice is only a problem.
segments.ipa: /wi stɑp ˈθɪŋkɪŋ ðæt ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈoʊnli ə ˈprɑbləm/

segments.text: We begin to see practice as the path itself.
segments.ipa: /wi bɪˈɡɪn tu si ˈpræktəs æz ðə pæθ ˌɪtˈsɛlf/

segments.text: This does not mean we forget our goals.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs dʌz nɑt min wi fərˈɡɛt ˈaʊər ɡoʊlz/

segments.text: Goals are useful.
segments.ipa: /ɡoʊlz ɑr ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: They give direction.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɡɪv dərˈɛkʃən/

segments.text: If you want to speak English fluently, the goal can guide you.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu spik ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluəntli ðə ɡoʊl kæn ɡaɪd ju/

segments.text: If you want to pass an exam, the goal can guide you.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu pæs æn ɪɡˈzæm ðə ɡoʊl kæn ɡaɪd ju/

segments.text: If you want to play a piece of music, the goal can help you.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu pleɪ ə pis ʌv ˈmjuzɪk ðə ɡoʊl kæn hɛlp ju/

segments.text: But the goal should not steal your peace.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ɡoʊl ʃʊd nɑt stil jɔr pis/

segments.text: A goal should point the way.
segments.ipa: /ə ɡoʊl ʃʊd pɔɪnt ðə weɪ/

segments.text: It should not make every step feel wrong.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ʃʊd nɑt meɪk ˈɛvəri stɛp fil rɔŋ/

segments.text: For example, imagine you are climbing a mountain.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˌɪˈmædʒən ju ɑr ˈklaɪmɪŋ ə ˈmaʊntən/

segments.text: The top of the mountain is your goal.
segments.ipa: /ðə tɑp ʌv ðə ˈmaʊntən ɪz jɔr ɡoʊl/

segments.text: But if you only look at the top, you may feel tired and frustrated.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju ˈoʊnli lʊk æt ðə tɑp ju meɪ fil ˈtaɪərd ənd ˈfrʌˌstreɪtəd/

segments.text: It looks far away.
segments.ipa: /ɪt lʊks fɑr əˈweɪ/

segments.text: It looks difficult.
segments.ipa: /ɪt lʊks ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: You may think, "I'm still not there."
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ θɪŋk aɪm stɪl nɑt ðɛr/

segments.text: But if you focus on the next step, climbing becomes possible.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə nɛkst stɛp ˈklaɪmɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: One step, then another step, then another one.
segments.ipa: /wʌn stɛp ðɛn əˈnʌðər stɛp ðɛn əˈnʌðər wʌn/

segments.text: Language learning is like this.
segments.ipa: /ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ ɪz laɪk ðɪs/

segments.text: Fluency is the mountain top.
segments.ipa: /ˈfluənsi ɪz ðə ˈmaʊntən tɑp/

segments.text: Today's listening is one step.
segments.ipa: /təˈdeɪz ˈlɪsənɪŋ ɪz wʌn stɛp/

segments.text: Today's speaking practice is one step.
segments.ipa: /təˈdeɪz ˈspikɪŋ ˈpræktəs ɪz wʌn stɛp/

segments.text: Today's vocabulary review is one step.
segments.ipa: /təˈdeɪz voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri ˌrivˈju ɪz wʌn stɛp/

segments.text: Today's mistake is also one step.
segments.ipa: /təˈdeɪz mɪˈsteɪk ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ wʌn stɛp/

segments.text: You climb through practice.
segments.ipa: /ju klaɪm θru ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Another important idea in this book is that practice trains the mind.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪn ðɪs bʊk ɪz ðæt ˈpræktəs treɪnz ðə maɪnd/

segments.text: Many people think practice only trains the skill.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl θɪŋk ˈpræktəs ˈoʊnli treɪnz ðə skɪl/

segments.text: For example, English practice trains English.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs treɪnz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Piano practice trains piano.
segments.ipa: /piˈænoʊ ˈpræktəs treɪnz piˈænoʊ/

segments.text: Exercise trains the body.
segments.ipa: /ˈɛksərˌsaɪz treɪnz ðə ˈbɑdi/

segments.text: But practice also trains your attitude.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈpræktəs ˈɔlsoʊ treɪnz jɔr ˈætəˌtud/

segments.text: It trains patience.
segments.ipa: /ɪt treɪnz ˈpeɪʃəns/

segments.text: It trains attention.
segments.ipa: /ɪt treɪnz əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: It trains emotional control.
segments.ipa: /ɪt treɪnz ɪˈmoʊʃənəl kənˈtroʊl/

segments.text: It trains discipline.
segments.ipa: /ɪt treɪnz ˈdɪsəplən/

segments.text: When you practice English slowly and carefully, you're not only learning English, you are learning how to stay with difficulty.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈpræktəs ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsloʊli ənd ˈkɛrfəli jʊr nɑt ˈoʊnli ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ haʊ tu steɪ wɪð ˈdɪfəkəlti/

segments.text: You're learning how not to run away.
segments.ipa: /jʊr ˈlɝnɪŋ haʊ nɑt tu rʌn əˈweɪ/

segments.text: You're learning how to continue without anger.
segments.ipa: /jʊr ˈlɝnɪŋ haʊ tu kənˈtɪnju wɪˈθaʊt ˈæŋɡər/

segments.text: You are learning how to be present.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ haʊ tu bi ˈprɛzənt/

segments.text: Present means here, now, in this moment.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛzənt minz hir naʊ ɪn ðɪs ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: The practicing mind is a mind that can stay in the present.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd ɪz ə maɪnd ðæt kæn steɪ ɪn ðə ˈprɛzənt/

segments.text: It does not always run to the future.
segments.ipa: /ɪt dʌz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz rʌn tu ðə ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: It does not always say, "When will I be finished?"
segments.ipa: /ɪt dʌz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz seɪ wɛn wɪl aɪ bi ˈfɪnɪʃt/

segments.text: It pays attention to what is happening now.
segments.ipa: /ɪt peɪz əˈtɛnʃən tu wʌt ɪz ˈhæpənɪŋ naʊ/

segments.text: It says, "This is my task.
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz ðɪs ɪz maɪ tæsk/

segments.text: I will do it carefully."
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl du ɪt ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: This is a peaceful way to learn.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈpisfəl weɪ tu lɝn/

segments.text: If you are repeating one English sentence, repeat that sentence.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ɑr rɪˈpitɪŋ wʌn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɛntəns rɪˈpit ðæt ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Do not think, "Why am I not fluent yet?"
segments.ipa: /du nɑt θɪŋk waɪ æm aɪ nɑt ˈfluənt jɛt/

segments.text: Just listen and repeat.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst ˈlɪsən ənd rɪˈpit/

segments.text: Feel the sound.
segments.ipa: /fil ðə saʊnd/

segments.text: Notice the rhythm and try again.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊtəs ðə ˈrɪðəm ənd traɪ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: If you're reading one paragraph, read that paragraph.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jʊr ˈridɪŋ wʌn ˈpærəˌɡræf rɛd ðæt ˈpærəˌɡræf/

segments.text: Do not think, "Why can't I read a whole book?"
segments.ipa: /du nɑt θɪŋk waɪ kænt aɪ rɛd ə hoʊl bʊk/

segments.text: Just read the words in front of you.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst rɛd ðə wɝdz ɪn frʌnt ʌv ju/

segments.text: If you are speaking for 1 minute, speak for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ɑr ˈspikɪŋ fɔr ˈmɪnət spik fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: Do not judge your whole English ability.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt dʒʌdʒ jɔr hoʊl ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ əˈbɪləˌti/

segments.text: Just practice this one small moment.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst ˈpræktəs ðɪs wʌn smɔl ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: This is the practicing mind.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd/

segments.text: So, in this episode, I will talk about process.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ɪn ðɪs ˈɛpəˌsoʊd aɪ wɪl tɔk əˈbaʊt ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: I will talk about patience, focus, discipline, present moment practice.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl tɔk əˈbaʊt ˈpeɪʃəns ˈfoʊkəs ˈdɪsəplən ˈprɛzənt ˈmoʊmənt ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: I will talk about mistakes, calm repetition, and how to enjoy learning.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl tɔk əˈbaʊt mɪˈsteɪks kɑm ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən ənd haʊ tu ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: I will connect the ideas from this book to English learning because language learning needs a practicing mind, too.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl kəˈnɛkt ðə aɪˈdiəz frʌm ðɪs bʊk tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnɪŋ bɪˈkɔz ˈlæŋɡwədʒ ˈlɝnɪŋ nidz ə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd tu/

segments.text: So, the first lesson from this book is simple.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə fɝst ˈlɛsən frʌm ðɪs bʊk ɪz ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: Do not hate practice.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt heɪt ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Practice is not the thing between you and success.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz nɑt ðə θɪŋ bɪˈtwin ju ənd səkˈsɛs/

segments.text: Practice is the thing that creates success.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz ðə θɪŋ ðæt kriˈeɪts səkˈsɛs/

segments.text: And when you learn to enjoy practice, the whole journey becomes lighter. All right.
segments.ipa: /ənd wɛn ju lɝn tu ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈpræktəs ðə hoʊl ˈdʒɝni bɪˈkʌmz ˈlaɪtər ɔl raɪt/

segments.text: One of the biggest ideas in this book is this.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ʌv ðə ˈbɪɡəst aɪˈdiəz ɪn ðɪs bʊk ɪz ðɪs/

segments.text: Focus on the process, not only on the product.
segments.ipa: /ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs nɑt ˈoʊnli ɑn ðə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: The product is the final result.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑdəkt ɪz ðə ˈfaɪnəl rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: It is what you want to have.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz wʌt ju wɑnt tu hæv/

segments.text: It is the finished thing.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ðə ˈfɪnɪʃt θɪŋ/

segments.text: For example, fluent English is a product.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ˈfluənt ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz ə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: A perfect performance is a product.
segments.ipa: /ə pərˈfɛkt pərˈfɔrməns ɪz ə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: A completed project is a product.
segments.ipa: /ə kəmˈplitəd ˈprɑdʒɛkt ɪz ə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: A high exam score is a product.
segments.ipa: /ə haɪ ɪɡˈzæm skɔr ɪz ə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: A successful business is a product.
segments.ipa: /ə səkˈsɛsfəl ˈbɪznəs ɪz ə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: The process is what creates the product.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz wʌt kriˈeɪts ðə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: The process is the daily practice, the small steps, the repetition, the listening, the speaking,
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ðə ˈdeɪli ˈpræktəs ðə smɔl stɛps ðə ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən ðə ˈlɪsənɪŋ ðə ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: the revealing, the correcting, and the trying again.
segments.ipa: /ðə rɪˈvilɪŋ ðə kərˈɛktɪŋ ənd ðə ˈtraɪɪŋ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Many people want the product, but they do not enjoy the process.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl wɑnt ðə ˈprɑdəkt bʌt ðeɪ du nɑt ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: This is why they suffer.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ðeɪ ˈsʌfər/

segments.text: They want the final result so much that every step feels too slow.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt ðə ˈfaɪnəl rɪˈzʌlt soʊ mʌtʃ ðæt ˈɛvəri stɛp filz tu sloʊ/

segments.text: They do not enjoy today because they're always thinking about tomorrow.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ du nɑt ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ təˈdeɪ bɪˈkɔz ðɛr ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt təˈmɑˌroʊ/

segments.text: For English learners, this is very common.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˈkɑmən/

segments.text: A learner says, "I want to speak English fluently."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈlɝnər sɛz aɪ wɑnt tu spik ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈfluəntli/

segments.text: This is a good goal, but then they listen to themselves speaking today and feel disappointed.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ɡʊd ɡoʊl bʌt ðɛn ðeɪ ˈlɪsən tu ðɛmˈsɛlvz ˈspikɪŋ təˈdeɪ ənd fil ˌdɪsəˈpɔɪntɪd/

segments.text: They say, "Well, my English is not fluent."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ wɛl maɪ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɪz nɑt ˈfluənt/

segments.text: They compare today's English with the dream.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ kəmˈpɛr təˈdeɪz ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ wɪð ðə drim/

segments.text: The dream is far away, so today feels bad.
segments.ipa: /ðə drim ɪz fɑr əˈweɪ soʊ təˈdeɪ filz bæd/

segments.text: But this is not a helpful way to learn.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðɪs ɪz nɑt ə ˈhɛlpfəl weɪ tu lɝn/

segments.text: The book teaches us to bring our attention back to the process.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈtitʃəz ʌs tu brɪŋ ˈaʊər əˈtɛnʃən bæk tu ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Instead of asking, "Am I fluent yet?"
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈæskɪŋ æm aɪ ˈfluənt jɛt/

segments.text: ask, "Did I practice today?"
segments.ipa: /æsk dɪd aɪ ˈpræktəs təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Instead of asking, "Why am I not advanced?"
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈæskɪŋ waɪ æm aɪ nɑt ədˈvænst/

segments.text: ask, "What small skill can I improve now?"
segments.ipa: /æsk wʌt smɔl skɪl kæn aɪ ˌɪmˈpruv naʊ/

segments.text: Instead of asking, "When will I finish?"
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd ʌv ˈæskɪŋ wɛn wɪl aɪ ˈfɪnɪʃ/

segments.text: ask, "Can I give full attention to this step?"
segments.ipa: /æsk kæn aɪ ɡɪv fʊl əˈtɛnʃən tu ðɪs stɛp/

segments.text: This changes everything.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ˈtʃeɪndʒəz ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: When you focus on the product, you feel pressure.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə ˈprɑdəkt ju fil ˈprɛʃər/

segments.text: You feel stress.
segments.ipa: /ju fil strɛs/

segments.text: When you focus on the process, you feel direction.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ju fil dərˈɛkʃən/

segments.text: Pressure says, "You must be there now."
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛʃər sɛz ju mʌst bi ðɛr naʊ/

segments.text: Direction says, "Take the next step."
segments.ipa: /dərˈɛkʃən sɛz teɪk ðə nɛkst stɛp/

segments.text: The process is always available.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ˈɔlˌweɪz əˈveɪləbəl/

segments.text: You may not be fluent today, but you can practice today.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ nɑt bi ˈfluənt təˈdeɪ bʌt ju kæn ˈpræktəs təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: You may not understand a whole movie today, but you can understand one short scene.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ nɑt ˌʌndərˈstænd ə hoʊl ˈmuvi təˈdeɪ bʌt ju kæn ˌʌndərˈstænd wʌn ʃɔrt sin/

segments.text: You may not speak perfectly today, but you can answer one simple question.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ nɑt spik ˈpɝfəktli təˈdeɪ bʌt ju kæn ˈænsər wʌn ˈsɪmpəl ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: You may not know many words today, but you can learn three useful phrases.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ nɑt noʊ ˈmɛni wɝdz təˈdeɪ bʌt ju kæn lɝn θri ˈjusfəl ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: So, the process is always available.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ˈɔlˌweɪz əˈveɪləbəl/

segments.text: And this is why process is powerful.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: It gives you something you can do now.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɡɪvz ju ˈsʌmθɪŋ ju kæn du naʊ/

segments.text: The product is in the future.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑdəkt ɪz ɪn ðə ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: The process is in your hands today.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ɪn jɔr hændz təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: The author explains that when we become too focused on the product, we become impatient.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɔθər ɪkˈspleɪnz ðæt wɛn wi bɪˈkʌm tu ˈfoʊkəst ɑn ðə ˈprɑdəkt wi bɪˈkʌm ˌɪmˈpeɪʃənt/

segments.text: We want to finish quickly. We rush.
segments.ipa: /wi wɑnt tu ˈfɪnɪʃ ˈkwɪkli wi rʌʃ/

segments.text: We become frustrated.
segments.ipa: /wi bɪˈkʌm ˈfrʌˌstreɪtəd/

segments.text: We do not enjoy the work.
segments.ipa: /wi du nɑt ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðə wɝk/

segments.text: We judge ourselves all the time.
segments.ipa: /wi dʒʌdʒ aʊərˈsɛlvz ɔl ðə taɪm/

segments.text: But real skill needs patience.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ril skɪl nidz ˈpeɪʃəns/

segments.text: Real skill grows slowly.
segments.ipa: /ril skɪl ɡroʊz ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: Real skill comes from repeating simple things with attention.
segments.ipa: /ril skɪl kʌmz frʌm rɪˈpitɪŋ ˈsɪmpəl θɪŋz wɪð əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: Think about pronunciation.
segments.ipa: /θɪŋk əˈbaʊt proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: You cannot improve pronunciation by being angry with your pronunciation.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt ˌɪmˈpruv proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən baɪ ˈbiɪŋ ˈæŋɡri wɪð jɔr proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən/

segments.text: You improve by listening, repeating, recording, correcting, and repeating again.
segments.ipa: /ju ˌɪmˈpruv baɪ ˈlɪsənɪŋ rɪˈpitɪŋ rəˈkɔrdɪŋ kərˈɛktɪŋ ənd rɪˈpitɪŋ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: The process is simple, but it needs patience.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ˈsɪmpəl bʌt ɪt nidz ˈpeɪʃəns/

segments.text: Think about speaking.
segments.ipa: /θɪŋk əˈbaʊt ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: You cannot become a confident speaker by waiting for perfect confidence.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt bɪˈkʌm ə ˈkɑnfədənt ˈspikər baɪ ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr pərˈfɛkt ˈkɑnfədəns/

segments.text: You become confident by speaking a little, feeling nervous, trying again, and slowly becoming more comfortable.
segments.ipa: /ju bɪˈkʌm ˈkɑnfədənt baɪ ˈspikɪŋ ə ˈlɪtəl ˈfilɪŋ ˈnɝvəs ˈtraɪɪŋ əˈɡɛn ənd ˈsloʊli bɪˈkʌmɪŋ mɔr ˈkʌmfərtəbəl/

segments.text: Think about vocabulary.
segments.ipa: /θɪŋk əˈbaʊt voʊˈkæbjəˌlɛri/

segments.text: You cannot own a word by seeing it once.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt oʊn ə wɝd baɪ ˈsiɪŋ ɪt wʌns/

segments.text: You need to meet it many times.
segments.ipa: /ju nid tu mit ɪt ˈmɛni taɪmz/

segments.text: You need to hear it many times.
segments.ipa: /ju nid tu hir ɪt ˈmɛni taɪmz/

segments.text: You need to read it, say it, use it, and review it.
segments.ipa: /ju nid tu rɛd ɪt seɪ ɪt jus ɪt ənd ˌrivˈju ɪt/

segments.text: This is process.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: A process-focused learner is calmer.
segments.ipa: /ə process-focused ˈlɝnər ɪz ˈkɑmər/

segments.text: They do not need every day to feel amazing.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ du nɑt nid ˈɛvəri deɪ tu fil əˈmeɪzɪŋ/

segments.text: They understand that practice is practice.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ˌʌndərˈstænd ðæt ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Some days are easy, some days are hard.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ɑr ˈizi sʌm deɪz ɑr hɑrd/

segments.text: Some days you feel progress, some days you feel slow.
segments.ipa: /sʌm deɪz ju fil ˈprɑˌɡrɛs sʌm deɪz ju fil sloʊ/

segments.text: But the process continues.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs kənˈtɪnjuz/

segments.text: This is very important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Process does not depend on mood.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɑˌsɛs dʌz nɑt dɪˈpɛnd ɑn mud/

segments.text: Mood means how you feel.
segments.ipa: /mud minz haʊ ju fil/

segments.text: If you only practice when your mood is good, your progress will be unstable.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈoʊnli ˈpræktəs wɛn jɔr mud ɪz ɡʊd jɔr ˈprɑˌɡrɛs wɪl bi ənˈsteɪbəl/

segments.text: But if you follow a process, you can practice even when you do not feel excited,
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju ˈfɑloʊ ə ˈprɑˌsɛs ju kæn ˈpræktəs ˈivɪn wɛn ju du nɑt fil ɪkˈsaɪtəd/

segments.text: so your progress will be stable.
segments.ipa: /soʊ jɔr ˈprɑˌɡrɛs wɪl bi ˈsteɪbəl/

segments.text: You can do the small step.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn du ðə smɔl stɛp/

segments.text: You can listen for 5 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈlɪsən fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: You can repeat one sentence.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn rɪˈpit wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: You can write one line.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn raɪt wʌn laɪn/

segments.text: A small process is better than no process.
segments.ipa: /ə smɔl ˈprɑˌsɛs ɪz ˈbɛtər ðæn noʊ ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: The book also helps us see that the product is not always under our control.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps ʌs si ðæt ðə ˈprɑdəkt ɪz nɑt ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈʌndər ˈaʊər kənˈtroʊl/

segments.text: You cannot fully control when you will become fluent.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt ˈfʊli kənˈtroʊl wɛn ju wɪl bɪˈkʌm ˈfluənt/

segments.text: You cannot control every exam result.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt kənˈtroʊl ˈɛvəri ɪɡˈzæm rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: You cannot control how fast your brain will absorb everything.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt kənˈtroʊl haʊ fæst jɔr breɪn wɪl əbˈzɔrb ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: You cannot control how other people judge you.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt kənˈtroʊl haʊ ˈʌðər ˈpipəl dʒʌdʒ ju/

segments.text: But you can control practice.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ju kæn kənˈtroʊl ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: You can control your attention.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn kənˈtroʊl jɔr əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: You can control today's step.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn kənˈtroʊl təˈdeɪz stɛp/

segments.text: This gives peace.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɡɪvz pis/

segments.text: A learner who only focuses on the product may feel helpless.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈlɝnər hu ˈoʊnli ˈfoʊkəsɪz ɑn ðə ˈprɑdəkt meɪ fil ˈhɛlpləs/

segments.text: They keep looking at the distance.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ kip ˈlʊkɪŋ æt ðə ˈdɪstəns/

segments.text: They say, "I'm still far away."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪm stɪl fɑr əˈweɪ/

segments.text: But a learner who focuses on the process says, "Today I can practice.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ə ˈlɝnər hu ˈfoʊkəsɪz ɑn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs sɛz təˈdeɪ aɪ kæn ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Today I can improve one small thing."
segments.ipa: /təˈdeɪ aɪ kæn ˌɪmˈpruv wʌn smɔl θɪŋ/

segments.text: That is a stronger mindset.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ə ˈstrɔŋər ˈmaɪndˌsɛt/

segments.text: Another important idea in the book is that when we focus on the process,
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪn ðə bʊk ɪz ðæt wɛn wi ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: we enjoy learning more.
segments.ipa: /wi ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈlɝnɪŋ mɔr/

segments.text: The daily practice becomes meaningful.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈdeɪli ˈpræktəs bɪˈkʌmz ˈminɪŋfəl/

segments.text: You start to feel satisfaction from doing the work, not only from finishing the work.
segments.ipa: /ju stɑrt tu fil ˌsætəsˈfækʃən frʌm ˈduɪŋ ðə wɝk nɑt ˈoʊnli frʌm ˈfɪnɪʃɪŋ ðə wɝk/

segments.text: For example, you may feel proud because you listened today.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ju meɪ fil praʊd bɪˈkɔz ju ˈlɪsənd təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: You may feel calm because you repeated a sentence carefully.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil kɑm bɪˈkɔz ju rɪˈpitɪd ə ˈsɛntəns ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: You may feel happy because you understood a phrase that was difficult before.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fil ˈhæpi bɪˈkɔz ju ˌʌndərˈstʊd ə freɪz ðæt wɑz ˈdɪfəkəlt bɪˈfɔr/

segments.text: The process becomes satisfying.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs bɪˈkʌmz ˈsætɪsˌfaɪɪŋ/

segments.text: This is important because the product may take a long time.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt bɪˈkɔz ðə ˈprɑdəkt meɪ teɪk ə lɔŋ taɪm/

segments.text: If you cannot enjoy the process, you may quit before the product arrives.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ˈkænɑt ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ju meɪ kwɪt bɪˈfɔr ðə ˈprɑdəkt ərˈaɪvz/

segments.text: But if you learn to enjoy the process, you can continue for many years.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju lɝn tu ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ju kæn kənˈtɪnju fɔr ˈmɛni jɪrz/

segments.text: This is how strong skills are built.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz haʊ strɔŋ skɪlz ɑr bɪlt/

segments.text: So, the lesson of this part of the book is clear.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈlɛsən ʌv ðɪs pɑrt ʌv ðə bʊk ɪz klɪr/

segments.text: Do not live only for the product.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt laɪv ˈoʊnli fɔr ðə ˈprɑdəkt/

segments.text: Respect the product, but love the process.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈspɛkt ðə ˈprɑdəkt bʌt lʌv ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: The result gives direction, but the process gives life.
segments.ipa: /ðə rɪˈzʌlt ɡɪvz dərˈɛkʃən bʌt ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ɡɪvz laɪf/

segments.text: The goal shows where to go, but practice is where you actually live.
segments.ipa: /ðə ɡoʊl ʃoʊz wɛr tu ɡoʊ bʌt ˈpræktəs ɪz wɛr ju ˈækˌtʃuəli laɪv/

segments.text: Your English grows in the process.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ɡroʊz ɪn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Your confidence grows in the process.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈkɑnfədəns ɡroʊz ɪn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Your discipline grows in the process.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈdɪsəplən ɡroʊz ɪn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Your practicing mind grows in the process.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd ɡroʊz ɪn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: So, today, do not ask only how far am I from fluency?
segments.ipa: /soʊ təˈdeɪ du nɑt æsk ˈoʊnli haʊ fɑr æm aɪ frʌm ˈfluənsi/

segments.text: Instead, ask, "What is my next small practice?
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd æsk wʌt ɪz maɪ nɛkst smɔl ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Then do it with attention.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn du ɪt wɪð əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: And that, my friend, would be your practice for today.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæt maɪ frɛnd wʊd bi jɔr ˈpræktəs fɔr təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: Another important idea in the practicing mind is presence.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪn ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd ɪz ˈprɛzəns/

segments.text: Presence means being here, being in this moment, paying attention to what you are doing now.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛzəns minz ˈbiɪŋ hir ˈbiɪŋ ɪn ðɪs ˈmoʊmənt ˈpeɪɪŋ əˈtɛnʃən tu wʌt ju ɑr ˈduɪŋ naʊ/

segments.text: This sounds simple, but it is difficult.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs saʊndz ˈsɪmpəl bʌt ɪt ɪz ˈdɪfəkəlt/

segments.text: Our mind likes to travel.
segments.ipa: /ˈaʊər maɪnd laɪks tu ˈtrævəl/

segments.text: It travels to the future.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈtrævəlz tu ðə ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: It says, "When will I be good?
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz wɛn wɪl aɪ bi ɡʊd/

segments.text: When will I finish?
segments.ipa: /wɛn wɪl aɪ ˈfɪnɪʃ/

segments.text: What if I fail?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf aɪ feɪl/

segments.text: What if people judge me?"
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf ˈpipəl dʒʌdʒ mi/

segments.text: It also travels to the past.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ˈɔlsoʊ ˈtrævəlz tu ðə pæst/

segments.text: It says, "I made mistakes before.
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz aɪ meɪd mɪˈsteɪks bɪˈfɔr/

segments.text: I failed before.
segments.ipa: /aɪ feɪld bɪˈfɔr/

segments.text: I was embarrassed before.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɑz ɪmˈbɛrəst bɪˈfɔr/

segments.text: I should have started earlier."
segments.ipa: /aɪ ʃʊd hæv ˈstɑrtɪd ˈɝliər/

segments.text: The mind moves everywhere, but practice happens only now.
segments.ipa: /ðə maɪnd muvz ˈɛvriˌwɛr bʌt ˈpræktəs ˈhæpənz ˈoʊnli naʊ/

segments.text: You cannot practice yesterday.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt ˈpræktəs ˈjɛstərˌdeɪ/

segments.text: You cannot practice tomorrow.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈkænɑt ˈpræktəs təˈmɑˌroʊ/

segments.text: You can only practice now.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈoʊnli ˈpræktəs naʊ/

segments.text: This is why presence is so important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz waɪ ˈprɛzəns ɪz soʊ ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: When you are present, your practice becomes deeper.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ɑr ˈprɛzənt jɔr ˈpræktəs bɪˈkʌmz ˈdipər/

segments.text: You hear more.
segments.ipa: /ju hir mɔr/

segments.text: You notice more.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈnoʊtəs mɔr/

segments.text: You learn more.
segments.ipa: /ju lɝn mɔr/

segments.text: You become calmer.
segments.ipa: /ju bɪˈkʌm ˈkɑmər/

segments.text: You stop fighting the moment.
segments.ipa: /ju stɑp ˈfaɪtɪŋ ðə ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: For English learners, being present means paying attention to the sentence you are hearing now.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ˈbiɪŋ ˈprɛzənt minz ˈpeɪɪŋ əˈtɛnʃən tu ðə ˈsɛntəns ju ɑr ˈhirɪŋ naʊ/

segments.text: Not worrying about the whole language.
segments.ipa: /nɑt ˈwɝiɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə hoʊl ˈlæŋɡwədʒ/

segments.text: Not judging your whole level.
segments.ipa: /nɑt ˈdʒʌdʒɪŋ jɔr hoʊl ˈlɛvəl/

segments.text: Just listening to this sentence.
segments.ipa: /dʒʌst ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu ðɪs ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Repeating this phrase.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈpitɪŋ ðɪs freɪz/

segments.text: Understanding this short part.
segments.ipa: /ˌʌndərˈstændɪŋ ðɪs ʃɔrt pɑrt/

segments.text: Speaking this answer one moment at a time.
segments.ipa: /ˈspikɪŋ ðɪs ˈænsər wʌn ˈmoʊmənt æt ə taɪm/

segments.text: Imagine you are shadowing an English sentence.
segments.ipa: /ˌɪˈmædʒən ju ɑr ˈʃædoʊɪŋ æn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Shadowing means you listen and repeat or you speak with the audio.
segments.ipa: /ˈʃædoʊɪŋ minz ju ˈlɪsən ənd rɪˈpit ɔr ju spik wɪð ðə ˈɑdiˌoʊ/

segments.text: If your mind is busy with fear, you may not hear the rhythm.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jɔr maɪnd ɪz ˈbɪzi wɪð fɪr ju meɪ nɑt hir ðə ˈrɪðəm/

segments.text: You may not notice the stress.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ nɑt ˈnoʊtəs ðə strɛs/

segments.text: You may only think, "My pronunciation is bad."
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ ˈoʊnli θɪŋk maɪ proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən ɪz bæd/

segments.text: But if you are present, you listen carefully.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju ɑr ˈprɛzənt ju ˈlɪsən ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: You notice the sound.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈnoʊtəs ðə saʊnd/

segments.text: You try again. You improve.
segments.ipa: /ju traɪ əˈɡɛn ju ˌɪmˈpruv/

segments.text: Presence makes practice better.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛzəns meɪks ˈpræktəs ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: So, the book suggests that many people create stress because they're not in the present.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə bʊk səˈdʒɛsts ðæt ˈmɛni ˈpipəl kriˈeɪt strɛs bɪˈkɔz ðɛr nɑt ɪn ðə ˈprɛzənt/

segments.text: They are doing one thing, but thinking about another thing.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈduɪŋ wʌn θɪŋ bʌt ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt əˈnʌðər θɪŋ/

segments.text: They are practicing, but thinking about the result.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈpræktəsɪŋ bʌt ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə rɪˈzʌlt/

segments.text: They are learning, but thinking about failure.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ bʌt ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ˈfeɪljər/

segments.text: They are working, but thinking about finishing.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ ɑr ˈwɝkɪŋ bʌt ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ˈfɪnɪʃɪŋ/

segments.text: This creates tension.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs kriˈeɪts ˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: Tension means tightness.
segments.ipa: /ˈtɛnʃən minz ˈtaɪtnəs/

segments.text: It can be in the body or the mind.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kæn bi ɪn ðə ˈbɑdi ɔr ðə maɪnd/

segments.text: When you are always trying to be somewhere else, the present feels uncomfortable.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ɑr ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈtraɪɪŋ tu bi ˈsʌmˌwɛr ɛls ðə ˈprɛzənt filz ənˈkʌmfərtəbəl/

segments.text: But if you accept the present, practice becomes peaceful.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju ækˈsɛpt ðə ˈprɛzənt ˈpræktəs bɪˈkʌmz ˈpisfəl/

segments.text: This does not mean practice is always easy.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs dʌz nɑt min ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈizi/

segments.text: It means you stop fighting the fact that practice is needed.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ju stɑp ˈfaɪtɪŋ ðə fækt ðæt ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈnidəd/

segments.text: For example, if you are a beginner, you are a beginner.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf ju ɑr ə bɪˈɡɪnər ju ɑr ə bɪˈɡɪnər/

segments.text: That is not a problem.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz nɑt ə ˈprɑbləm/

segments.text: It is the current moment.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ðə ˈkɝənt ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: If you make a mistake, you made a mistake.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju meɪk ə mɪˈsteɪk ju meɪd ə mɪˈsteɪk/

segments.text: That is not the end.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz nɑt ðə ɛnd/

segments.text: It is information.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/

segments.text: If you need to repeat something 10 times, you need to repeat it 10 times.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju nid tu rɪˈpit ˈsʌmθɪŋ taɪmz ju nid tu rɪˈpit ɪt taɪmz/

segments.text: That is the process.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: Presence says, "This is where I am.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛzəns sɛz ðɪs ɪz wɛr aɪ æm/

segments.text: This is what I'm doing.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz wʌt aɪm ˈduɪŋ/

segments.text: I will give attention to this step."
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl ɡɪv əˈtɛnʃən tu ðɪs stɛp/

segments.text: And that is very powerful.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæt ɪz ˈvɛri ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: A present learner does not say, "I should already be fluent."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɝnər dʌz nɑt seɪ aɪ ʃʊd ɔlˈrɛdi bi ˈfluənt/

segments.text: A present learner says, "Today, I am practicing this sentence."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɝnər sɛz təˈdeɪ aɪ æm ˈpræktəsɪŋ ðɪs ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: A present learner does not say, "I hate being slow."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɝnər dʌz nɑt seɪ aɪ heɪt ˈbiɪŋ sloʊ/

segments.text: A present learner says, "Slow practice helps me learn."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɝnər sɛz sloʊ ˈpræktəs hɛlps mi lɝn/

segments.text: A present learner does not say, "I must finish quickly."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɝnər dʌz nɑt seɪ aɪ mʌst ˈfɪnɪʃ ˈkwɪkli/

segments.text: A present learner says, "Let me do this carefully."
segments.ipa: /ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɝnər sɛz lɛt mi du ðɪs ˈkɛrfəli/

segments.text: Careful practice is often better than rushed practice.
segments.ipa: /ˈkɛrfəl ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈɔfən ˈbɛtər ðæn rʌʃt ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: This is true for speaking, too.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz tru fɔr ˈspikɪŋ tu/

segments.text: Many learners rush because they want to sound fluent.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz rʌʃ bɪˈkɔz ðeɪ wɑnt tu saʊnd ˈfluənt/

segments.text: They speak too fast.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ spik tu fæst/

segments.text: Then, they make more mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ meɪk mɔr mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Their pronunciation becomes unclear.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən bɪˈkʌmz ənˈklɪr/

segments.text: Their ideas become messy.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr aɪˈdiəz bɪˈkʌm ˈmɛsi/

segments.text: But, if they slow down and speak with presence, they often sound better.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ðeɪ sloʊ daʊn ənd spik wɪð ˈprɛzəns ðeɪ ˈɔfən saʊnd ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: Fluency is not only speak, fluency is flow.
segments.ipa: /ˈfluənsi ɪz nɑt ˈoʊnli spik ˈfluənsi ɪz floʊ/

segments.text: A person can speak slowly and clearly and still communicate well.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈpɝsən kæn spik ˈsloʊli ənd ˈklɪrli ənd stɪl kəmˈjunəˌkeɪt wɛl/

segments.text: So, do not rush. Be present.
segments.ipa: /soʊ du nɑt rʌʃ bi ˈprɛzənt/

segments.text: Say one sentence clearly.
segments.ipa: /seɪ wʌn ˈsɛntəns ˈklɪrli/

segments.text: Then, another sentence, and then another one.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn əˈnʌðər ˈsɛntəns ənd ðɛn əˈnʌðər wʌn/

segments.text: For example, I think daily practice is important. Pause.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl aɪ θɪŋk ˈdeɪli ˈpræktəs ɪz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt pɔz/

segments.text: It helps your brain remember English. Pause.
segments.ipa: /ɪt hɛlps jɔr breɪn rɪˈmɛmbər ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ pɔz/

segments.text: Listening every morning can improve your listening. Pause. You see?
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈɛvəri ˈmɔrnɪŋ kæn ˌɪmˈpruv jɔr ˈlɪsənɪŋ pɔz ju si/

segments.text: This is clear, calm speaking practice.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz klɪr kɑm ˈspikɪŋ ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: You say sentence, you pause, and you give yourself time.
segments.ipa: /ju seɪ ˈsɛntəns ju pɔz ənd ju ɡɪv jərˈsɛlf taɪm/

segments.text: Presence also helps with listening.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛzəns ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps wɪð ˈlɪsənɪŋ/

segments.text: Many learners panic when they miss one word.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz ˈpænɪk wɛn ðeɪ mɪs wʌn wɝd/

segments.text: They hear one unknown word and think, "Ah, I don't understand anything."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ hir wʌn ənˈnoʊn wɝd ənd θɪŋk ɑ aɪ doʊnt ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈɛniˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: Then they stop listening.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ stɑp ˈlɪsənɪŋ/

segments.text: But a present listener continues.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ə ˈprɛzənt ˈlɪsənər kənˈtɪnjuz/

segments.text: They say, "Well, I missed that word, but I can still understand the main idea."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ wɛl aɪ mɪst ðæt wɝd bʌt aɪ kæn stɪl ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə meɪn aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: They stay with the audio.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ steɪ wɪð ðə ˈɑdiˌoʊ/

segments.text: And that, my friend, is a skill.
segments.ipa: /ənd ðæt maɪ frɛnd ɪz ə skɪl/

segments.text: Do not let one missed word take you out of the moment. Stay present.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt lɛt wʌn mɪst wɝd teɪk ju aʊt ʌv ðə ˈmoʊmənt steɪ ˈprɛzənt/

segments.text: Listen for what you can understand, then listen again.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən fɔr wʌt ju kæn ˌʌndərˈstænd ðɛn ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: The practicing mind is patient because it knows that every repetition is useful.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd ɪz ˈpeɪʃənt bɪˈkɔz ɪt noʊz ðæt ˈɛvəri ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən ɪz ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: So, be patient.
segments.ipa: /soʊ bi ˈpeɪʃənt/

segments.text: When you repeat a sentence, you're not wasting time.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju rɪˈpit ə ˈsɛntəns jʊr nɑt ˈweɪstɪŋ taɪm/

segments.text: You are training.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr ˈtreɪnɪŋ/

segments.text: When you listen again, you are not failing.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn ju ɑr nɑt ˈfeɪlɪŋ/

segments.text: You are learning deeper.
segments.ipa: /ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈdipər/

segments.text: Repetition is not a sign that you are weak.
segments.ipa: /ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən ɪz nɑt ə saɪn ðæt ju ɑr wik/

segments.text: Repetition is how skill grows.
segments.ipa: /ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən ɪz haʊ skɪl ɡroʊz/

segments.text: Presence also helps with anxiety.
segments.ipa: /ˈprɛzəns ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps wɪð æŋˈzaɪəti/

segments.text: Anxiety often comes from future thinking.
segments.ipa: /æŋˈzaɪəti ˈɔfən kʌmz frʌm ˈfjutʃər ˈθɪŋkɪŋ/

segments.text: What if I fail?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf aɪ feɪl/

segments.text: What if I forget?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf aɪ fərˈɡɛt/

segments.text: What if I sound stupid?
segments.ipa: /wʌt ɪf aɪ saʊnd ˈstupəd/

segments.text: These questions are about the future.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈkwɛstʃənz ɑr əˈbaʊt ðə ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: They may not happen, but your body reacts as if they are happening now.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ meɪ nɑt ˈhæpən bʌt jɔr ˈbɑdi riˈækts æz ɪf ðeɪ ɑr ˈhæpənɪŋ naʊ/

segments.text: To come back to the present, focus on a small action.
segments.ipa: /tu kʌm bæk tu ðə ˈprɛzənt ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ə smɔl ˈækʃən/

segments.text: Take one breath.
segments.ipa: /teɪk wʌn brɛθ/

segments.text: Listen to one sentence.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən tu wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Say one phrase.
segments.ipa: /seɪ wʌn freɪz/

segments.text: Write one word.
segments.ipa: /raɪt wʌn wɝd/

segments.text: Answer one question.
segments.ipa: /ˈænsər wʌn ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: Small actions bring the mind back.
segments.ipa: /smɔl ˈækʃənz brɪŋ ðə maɪnd bæk/

segments.text: For English practice, you can use this sentence.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs ju kæn jus ðɪs ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Right now, I only need to practice this.
segments.ipa: /raɪt naʊ aɪ ˈoʊnli nid tu ˈpræktəs ðɪs/

segments.text: This is a calming sentence.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈkɑmɪŋ ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Right now, I only need to listen.
segments.ipa: /raɪt naʊ aɪ ˈoʊnli nid tu ˈlɪsən/

segments.text: Right now, I only need to repeat.
segments.ipa: /raɪt naʊ aɪ ˈoʊnli nid tu rɪˈpit/

segments.text: Right now, I only need to speak for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /raɪt naʊ aɪ ˈoʊnli nid tu spik fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: Right now, I only need to try again.
segments.ipa: /raɪt naʊ aɪ ˈoʊnli nid tu traɪ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: This helps reduce pressure.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs hɛlps rəˈdus ˈprɛʃər/

segments.text: The book reminds us that practice is not something to rush through.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk riˈmaɪndz ʌs ðæt ˈpræktəs ɪz nɑt ˈsʌmθɪŋ tu rʌʃ θru/

segments.text: Practice is where we live.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz wɛr wi laɪv/

segments.text: If we are always waiting for the future, we miss the life inside today.
segments.ipa: /ɪf wi ɑr ˈɔlˌweɪz ˈweɪtɪŋ fɔr ðə ˈfjutʃər wi mɪs ðə laɪf ˌɪnˈsaɪd təˈdeɪ/

segments.text: This is true beyond English.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz tru bɪˈɑnd ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: It is true in music, work, relationships, health, and personal growth.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz tru ɪn ˈmjuzɪk wɝk riˈleɪʃənˌʃɪps hɛlθ ənd ˈpɝsɪnəl ɡroʊθ/

segments.text: The present moment is the only place where change happens.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈprɛzənt ˈmoʊmənt ɪz ðə ˈoʊnli pleɪs wɛr tʃeɪndʒ ˈhæpənz/

segments.text: So, the lesson of this part is simple.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈlɛsən ʌv ðɪs pɑrt ɪz ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: Be present while you practice.
segments.ipa: /bi ˈprɛzənt waɪl ju ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Give attention to the step in front of you.
segments.ipa: /ɡɪv əˈtɛnʃən tu ðə stɛp ɪn frʌnt ʌv ju/

segments.text: Do not fight your current level.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt faɪt jɔr ˈkɝənt ˈlɛvəl/

segments.text: Do not rush.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt rʌʃ/

segments.text: Do not judge every second.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt dʒʌdʒ ˈɛvəri ˈsɛkənd/

segments.text: Listen, repeat, notice, and try again.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən rɪˈpit ˈnoʊtəs ənd traɪ əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Your mind will run away sometimes.
segments.ipa: /jɔr maɪnd wɪl rʌn əˈweɪ səmˈtaɪmz/

segments.text: That is normal.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˈnɔrməl/

segments.text: Gently bring it back.
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒɛntli brɪŋ ɪt bæk/

segments.text: One sentence, one breath, one step.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ˈsɛntəns wʌn brɛθ wʌn stɛp/

segments.text: This is the practicing mind.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd/

segments.text: Now, many people hear the word discipline and think of something hard.
segments.ipa: /naʊ ˈmɛni ˈpipəl hir ðə wɝd ˈdɪsəplən ənd θɪŋk ʌv ˈsʌmθɪŋ hɑrd/

segments.text: They think discipline means forcing yourself, pushing yourself, being strict, feeling guilty, working even when you hate it.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk ˈdɪsəplən minz ˈfɔrsɪŋ jərˈsɛlf ˈpʊʃɪŋ jərˈsɛlf ˈbiɪŋ strɪkt ˈfilɪŋ ˈɡɪlti ˈwɝkɪŋ ˈivɪn wɛn ju heɪt ɪt/

segments.text: But the book gives us a calmer idea of discipline.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə bʊk ɡɪvz ʌs ə ˈkɑmər aɪˈdiə ʌv ˈdɪsəplən/

segments.text: Discipline does not have to be stressful.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən dʌz nɑt hæv tu bi ˈstrɛsfəl/

segments.text: Discipline can be peaceful.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən kæn bi ˈpisfəl/

segments.text: Discipline can simply mean doing the next right thing with attention.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən kæn ˈsɪmpli min ˈduɪŋ ðə nɛkst raɪt θɪŋ wɪð əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: It means staying with the process.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz ˈsteɪɪŋ wɪð ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: It means returning to practice.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz rɪˈtɝnɪŋ tu ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: It means not letting every emotion control your action.
segments.ipa: /ɪt minz nɑt ˈlɛtɪŋ ˈɛvəri ɪˈmoʊʃən kənˈtroʊl jɔr ˈækʃən/

segments.text: This is important because many learners have a painful relationship with discipline.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt bɪˈkɔz ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz hæv ə ˈpeɪnfəl riˈleɪʃənˌʃɪp wɪð ˈdɪsəplən/

segments.text: They say, "I must study.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪ mʌst ˈstʌdi/

segments.text: I should be better.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ʃʊd bi ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: I am lazy.
segments.ipa: /aɪ æm ˈleɪzi/

segments.text: I never do enough."
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˈnɛvər du ɪˈnʌf/

segments.text: This creates shame.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs kriˈeɪts ʃeɪm/

segments.text: And shame does not help learning.
segments.ipa: /ənd ʃeɪm dʌz nɑt hɛlp ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: A better kind of discipline is gentle and steady.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈbɛtər kaɪnd ʌv ˈdɪsəplən ɪz ˈdʒɛntəl ənd ˈstɛdi/

segments.text: Gentle means kind.
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒɛntəl minz kaɪnd/

segments.text: Steady means stable and regular.
segments.ipa: /ˈstɛdi minz ˈsteɪbəl ənd ˈrɛɡjələr/

segments.text: Gentle discipline says, "I will practice today, but I will not attack myself.
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒɛntəl ˈdɪsəplən sɛz aɪ wɪl ˈpræktəs təˈdeɪ bʌt aɪ wɪl nɑt əˈtæk ˌmaɪˈsɛlf/

segments.text: It says, I will take this seriously, but I will stay calm.
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz aɪ wɪl teɪk ðɪs ˈsɪriəsli bʌt aɪ wɪl steɪ kɑm/

segments.text: It says, I will return to the habit even after a bad day.
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz aɪ wɪl rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈhæbət ˈivɪn ˈæftər ə bæd deɪ/

segments.text: This kind of discipline lasts longer.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs kaɪnd ʌv ˈdɪsəplən læsts ˈlɔŋɡər/

segments.text: The book teaches that when we focus on the process, discipline becomes easier. Why?
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈtitʃəz ðæt wɛn wi ˈfoʊkəs ɑn ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs ˈdɪsəplən bɪˈkʌmz ˈiziər waɪ/

segments.text: Because the task becomes smaller.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈkɔz ðə tæsk bɪˈkʌmz ˈsmɔlər/

segments.text: You're not thinking about the whole future.
segments.ipa: /jʊr nɑt ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt ðə hoʊl ˈfjutʃər/

segments.text: You're only doing the step in front of you.
segments.ipa: /jʊr ˈoʊnli ˈduɪŋ ðə stɛp ɪn frʌnt ʌv ju/

segments.text: For example, if you think, I must become fluent, the goal feels huge.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf ju θɪŋk aɪ mʌst bɪˈkʌm ˈfluənt ðə ɡoʊl filz hjudʒ/

segments.text: But if you think, I will listen for 10 minutes, the action feels possible.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju θɪŋk aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən fɔr ˈmɪnəts ðə ˈækʃən filz ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: Discipline is easier when the action is clear and small.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən ɪz ˈiziər wɛn ðə ˈækʃən ɪz klɪr ənd smɔl/

segments.text: Do not discipline yourself with big pressure.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt ˈdɪsəplən jərˈsɛlf wɪð bɪɡ ˈprɛʃər/

segments.text: Guide yourself with small actions.
segments.ipa: /ɡaɪd jərˈsɛlf wɪð smɔl ˈækʃənz/

segments.text: For English learners, this means creating simple routines.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz ðɪs minz kriˈeɪtɪŋ ˈsɪmpəl ruˈtinz/

segments.text: Maybe every morning after coffee, you listen to English for 10 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈɛvəri ˈmɔrnɪŋ ˈæftər ˈkɑfi ju ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: Maybe every night before sleep, you review five phrases.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈɛvəri naɪt bɪˈfɔr slip ju ˌrivˈju faɪv ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: Maybe every afternoon, you speak for 1 minute about your day.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ˈɛvəri ˌæftərˈnun ju spik fɔr ˈmɪnət əˈbaʊt jɔr deɪ/

segments.text: These actions are not dramatic, but if you repeat them, they become powerful.
segments.ipa: /ðiz ˈækʃənz ɑr nɑt drəˈmætɪk bʌt ɪf ju rɪˈpit ðɛm ðeɪ bɪˈkʌm ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: So, discipline is not one heroic day.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˈdɪsəplən ɪz nɑt wʌn hɪˈroʊɪk deɪ/

segments.text: Discipline is returning again and again, repeating again and again.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən ɪz rɪˈtɝnɪŋ əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn rɪˈpitɪŋ əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Another important idea is that discipline grows when we remove unnecessary emotion from practice.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə ɪz ðæt ˈdɪsəplən ɡroʊz wɛn wi riˈmuv ənˈnɛsəˌsɛri ɪˈmoʊʃən frʌm ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Sometimes we make practice too emotional.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi meɪk ˈpræktəs tu ɪˈmoʊʃənəl/

segments.text: If it goes well, we feel excited.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ɪt ɡoʊz wɛl wi fil ɪkˈsaɪtəd/

segments.text: If practice goes badly, we feel terrible.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈpræktəs ɡoʊz ˈbædli wi fil ˈtɛrəbəl/

segments.text: If we miss one day, we feel like failures.
segments.ipa: /ɪf wi mɪs wʌn deɪ wi fil laɪk ˈfeɪljərz/

segments.text: If we make one mistake, we feel hopeless.
segments.ipa: /ɪf wi meɪk wʌn mɪˈsteɪk wi fil ˈhoʊpləs/

segments.text: This emotional roller coaster makes learning hard.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪˈmoʊʃənəl ˈroʊlər ˈkoʊstər meɪks ˈlɝnɪŋ hɑrd/

segments.text: A roller coaster goes up and down quickly.
segments.ipa: /ə ˈroʊlər ˈkoʊstər ɡoʊz ʌp ənd daʊn ˈkwɪkli/

segments.text: Emotional practice is like that.
segments.ipa: /ɪˈmoʊʃənəl ˈpræktəs ɪz laɪk ðæt/

segments.text: One day you feel high, one day you feel low.
segments.ipa: /wʌn deɪ ju fil haɪ wʌn deɪ ju fil loʊ/

segments.text: You depend too much on feelings.
segments.ipa: /ju dɪˈpɛnd tu mʌtʃ ɑn ˈfilɪŋz/

segments.text: The practicing mind is more stable.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd ɪz mɔr ˈsteɪbəl/

segments.text: It says, "Today's practice is today's practice.
segments.ipa: /ɪt sɛz təˈdeɪz ˈpræktəs ɪz təˈdeɪz ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Some parts were good, some parts need work.
segments.ipa: /sʌm pɑrts wɝ ɡʊd sʌm pɑrts nid wɝk/

segments.text: I will continue."
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl kənˈtɪnju/

segments.text: This is calm.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz kɑm/

segments.text: For example, if you listen to a podcast and understand only 50%, you do not need to panic.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl ɪf ju ˈlɪsən tu ə ˈpɔdˌkæst ənd ˌʌndərˈstænd ˈoʊnli ju du nɑt nid tu ˈpænɪk/

segments.text: You can say, "Good.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn seɪ ɡʊd/

segments.text: I understood some of it.
segments.ipa: /aɪ ˌʌndərˈstʊd sʌm ʌv ɪt/

segments.text: I will listen again."
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: If you speak and make mistakes, you can say, "Good.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju spik ənd meɪk mɪˈsteɪks ju kæn seɪ ɡʊd/

segments.text: Now I know what to practice."
segments.ipa: /naʊ aɪ noʊ wʌt tu ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: If you feel tired and only practice 5 minutes, you can say, "Good.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju fil ˈtaɪərd ənd ˈoʊnli ˈpræktəs ˈmɪnəts ju kæn seɪ ɡʊd/

segments.text: I kept the habit alive."
segments.ipa: /aɪ kɛpt ðə ˈhæbət əˈlaɪv/

segments.text: This is discipline without drama.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈdɪsəplən wɪˈθaʊt ˈdrɑmə/

segments.text: Drama makes learning heavy.
segments.ipa: /ˈdrɑmə meɪks ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈhɛvi/

segments.text: Calm practice makes learning possible.
segments.ipa: /kɑm ˈpræktəs meɪks ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: The author also teaches that we should not judge ourselves constantly.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈɔθər ˈɔlsoʊ ˈtitʃəz ðæt wi ʃʊd nɑt dʒʌdʒ aʊərˈsɛlvz ˈkɑnstəntli/

segments.text: Judgment is when we keep saying, "This is good.
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒʌdʒmənt ɪz wɛn wi kip ˈseɪɪŋ ðɪs ɪz ɡʊd/

segments.text: This is bad. I'm good. I'm bad."
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz bæd aɪm ɡʊd aɪm bæd/

segments.text: Of course, we need to notice mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ʌv kɔrs wi nid tu ˈnoʊtəs mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: But constant judgment creates tension.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈkɑnstənt ˈdʒʌdʒmənt kriˈeɪts ˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: There is a difference between observation and judgment.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ɪz ə ˈdɪfərəns bɪˈtwin ˌɑbzərˈveɪʃən ənd ˈdʒʌdʒmənt/

segments.text: Observation says, "I missed this word."
segments.ipa: /ˌɑbzərˈveɪʃən sɛz aɪ mɪst ðɪs wɝd/

segments.text: Judgment says, "I am terrible at listening."
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒʌdʒmənt sɛz aɪ æm ˈtɛrəbəl æt ˈlɪsənɪŋ/

segments.text: Observation says, "My pronunciation of this sound needs practice."
segments.ipa: /ˌɑbzərˈveɪʃən sɛz maɪ proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən ʌv ðɪs saʊnd nidz ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Judgment says, "My accent is awful." Observation helps. Judgment hurts.
segments.ipa: /ˈdʒʌdʒmənt sɛz maɪ əkˈsɛnt ɪz ˈɑfəl ˌɑbzərˈveɪʃən hɛlps ˈdʒʌdʒmənt hɝts/

segments.text: The practicing mind observes. It notices. It corrects. It continues.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd əbˈzɝvz ɪt ˈnoʊtəsəz ɪt kərˈɛkts ɪt kənˈtɪnjuz/

segments.text: This is a very useful habit for English practice.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈvɛri ˈjusfəl ˈhæbət fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: When you record your voice, listen like a teacher, not like an enemy.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju rəˈkɔrd jɔr vɔɪs ˈlɪsən laɪk ə ˈtitʃər nɑt laɪk æn ˈɛnəmi/

segments.text: Do not say, "I hate my voice."
segments.ipa: /du nɑt seɪ aɪ heɪt maɪ vɔɪs/

segments.text: Say, "What can I improve?"
segments.ipa: /seɪ wʌt kæn aɪ ˌɪmˈpruv/

segments.text: Maybe the answer is stress.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðə ˈænsər ɪz strɛs/

segments.text: Maybe the answer is rhythm.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ðə ˈænsər ɪz ˈrɪðəm/

segments.text: Maybe it is one sound.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ɪt ɪz wʌn saʊnd/

segments.text: Maybe it is pausing more.
segments.ipa: /ˈmeɪbi ɪt ɪz ˈpɔzɪŋ mɔr/

segments.text: Choose one thing and practice it.
segments.ipa: /tʃuz wʌn θɪŋ ənd ˈpræktəs ɪt/

segments.text: This is disciplined learning.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈdɪsəplənd ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Discipline also means finishing the small action you planned.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən ˈɔlsoʊ minz ˈfɪnɪʃɪŋ ðə smɔl ˈækʃən ju plænd/

segments.text: Not because you are afraid.
segments.ipa: /nɑt bɪˈkɔz ju ɑr əˈfreɪd/

segments.text: Not because you hate yourself.
segments.ipa: /nɑt bɪˈkɔz ju heɪt jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: But because you respect yourself.
segments.ipa: /bʌt bɪˈkɔz ju rɪˈspɛkt jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: If you say, "I will listen for 5 minutes."
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju seɪ aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: Listen for 5 minutes.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: If you say, "I will repeat one sentence."
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju seɪ aɪ wɪl rɪˈpit wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Repeat one sentence.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈpit wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Keeping small promises builds self-trust.
segments.ipa: /ˈkipɪŋ smɔl ˈprɑməsəz bɪldz self-trust/

segments.text: Self-trust means you believe your own word.
segments.ipa: /Self-trust minz ju bɪˈliv jɔr oʊn wɝd/

segments.text: This is very important.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt/

segments.text: Many learners break promises to themselves because the promises are too big.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz breɪk ˈprɑməsəz tu ðɛmˈsɛlvz bɪˈkɔz ðə ˈprɑməsəz ɑr tu bɪɡ/

segments.text: They say, "I will study 2 hours every day."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ seɪ aɪ wɪl ˈstʌdi ˈaʊərz ˈɛvəri deɪ/

segments.text: Then they stop.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ stɑp/

segments.text: Then they feel bad.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn ðeɪ fil bæd/

segments.text: Instead, make a smaller promise and keep it.
segments.ipa: /ˌɪnˈstɛd meɪk ə ˈsmɔlər ˈprɑməs ənd kip ɪt/

segments.text: For example, "I will listen for 5 minutes.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ɪɡˈzæmpəl aɪ wɪl ˈlɪsən fɔr ˈmɪnəts/

segments.text: I will speak for 1 minute.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl spik fɔr ˈmɪnət/

segments.text: I will write one sentence.
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl raɪt wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: I will review three phrases."
segments.ipa: /aɪ wɪl ˌrivˈju θri ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: These small promises are easy to keep.
segments.ipa: /ðiz smɔl ˈprɑməsəz ɑr ˈizi tu kip/

segments.text: And when you keep them, you feel stronger.
segments.ipa: /ənd wɛn ju kip ðɛm ju fil ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: You begin to think, "I can trust myself."
segments.ipa: /ju bɪˈɡɪn tu θɪŋk aɪ kæn trʌst ˌmaɪˈsɛlf/

segments.text: This is discipline, not pressure, not shame. Trust.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈdɪsəplən nɑt ˈprɛʃər nɑt ʃeɪm trʌst/

segments.text: Another part of discipline is returning after distraction.
segments.ipa: /əˈnʌðər pɑrt ʌv ˈdɪsəplən ɪz rɪˈtɝnɪŋ ˈæftər dɪˈstrækʃən/

segments.text: You will get distracted. Everyone does.
segments.ipa: /ju wɪl ɡɛt dɪˈstræktəd ˈɛvriˌwʌn dʌz/

segments.text: Your mind will run away.
segments.ipa: /jɔr maɪnd wɪl rʌn əˈweɪ/

segments.text: Your phone will call you.
segments.ipa: /jɔr foʊn wɪl kɔl ju/

segments.text: Your mood will change.
segments.ipa: /jɔr mud wɪl tʃeɪndʒ/

segments.text: You may forget.
segments.ipa: /ju meɪ fərˈɡɛt/

segments.text: Question is not, "Can I be perfect?"
segments.ipa: /ˈkwɛstʃən ɪz nɑt kæn aɪ bi pərˈfɛkt/

segments.text: The question is, "Can I return?"
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈkwɛstʃən ɪz kæn aɪ rɪˈtɝn/

segments.text: Return to the sentence.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Return to the audio.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈɑdiˌoʊ/

segments.text: Return to the notebook.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈnoʊtˌbʊk/

segments.text: Return to the habit.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈhæbət/

segments.text: Return to the present moment.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈprɛzənt ˈmoʊmənt/

segments.text: This is the practicing mind.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd/

segments.text: So, the lesson of this part is simple.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈlɛsən ʌv ðɪs pɑrt ɪz ˈsɪmpəl/

segments.text: Discipline does not need to feel harsh.
segments.ipa: /ˈdɪsəplən dʌz nɑt nid tu fil hɑrʃ/

segments.text: Real discipline can be calm, gentle, and steady.
segments.ipa: /ril ˈdɪsəplən kæn bi kɑm ˈdʒɛntəl ənd ˈstɛdi/

segments.text: It is doing the next small action.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈduɪŋ ðə nɛkst smɔl ˈækʃən/

segments.text: It is observing without attacking yourself.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz əbˈzɝvɪŋ wɪˈθaʊt əˈtækɪŋ jərˈsɛlf/

segments.text: It is keeping small promises.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈkipɪŋ smɔl ˈprɑməsəz/

segments.text: It is returning when you drift away.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz rɪˈtɝnɪŋ wɛn ju drɪft əˈweɪ/

segments.text: You do not need to fight yourself to learn English.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid tu faɪt jərˈsɛlf tu lɝn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: You need to guide yourself with patience, with attention, with calm discipline. Okay.
segments.ipa: /ju nid tu ɡaɪd jərˈsɛlf wɪð ˈpeɪʃəns wɪð əˈtɛnʃən wɪð kɑm ˈdɪsəplən ˌoʊˈkeɪ/

segments.text: One of the most surprising ideas in the book is that slowing down can help you improve faster.
segments.ipa: /wʌn ʌv ðə moʊst sərˈpraɪzɪŋ aɪˈdiəz ɪn ðə bʊk ɪz ðæt ˈsloʊɪŋ daʊn kæn hɛlp ju ˌɪmˈpruv ˈfæstər/

segments.text: At first, this sounds strange.
segments.ipa: /æt fɝst ðɪs saʊndz streɪndʒ/

segments.text: Many people think faster is better.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl θɪŋk ˈfæstər ɪz ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: They want to learn fast, speak fast, finish fast, improve fast.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt tu lɝn fæst spik fæst ˈfɪnɪʃ fæst ˌɪmˈpruv fæst/

segments.text: They want quick results.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt kwɪk rɪˈzʌlts/

segments.text: They want to move quickly from beginner to advanced.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ wɑnt tu muv ˈkwɪkli frʌm bɪˈɡɪnər tu ədˈvænst/

segments.text: But in many skills, rushing creates mistakes.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪn ˈmɛni skɪlz ˈrʌʃɪŋ kriˈeɪts mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Rushing makes the mind tense.
segments.ipa: /ˈrʌʃɪŋ meɪks ðə maɪnd tɛns/

segments.text: Rushing makes the body tight.
segments.ipa: /ˈrʌʃɪŋ meɪks ðə ˈbɑdi taɪt/

segments.text: Rushing stops you from noticing details and details matter.
segments.ipa: /ˈrʌʃɪŋ stɑps ju frʌm ˈnoʊtɪsɪŋ dɪˈteɪlz ənd dɪˈteɪlz ˈmætər/

segments.text: Slow practice is powerful because it gives your mind time to think, time to notice.
segments.ipa: /sloʊ ˈpræktəs ɪz ˈpaʊərfəl bɪˈkɔz ɪt ɡɪvz jɔr maɪnd taɪm tu θɪŋk taɪm tu ˈnoʊtəs/

segments.text: When you slow down, you can hear the sound.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju sloʊ daʊn ju kæn hir ðə saʊnd/

segments.text: You can feel the rhythm.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn fil ðə ˈrɪðəm/

segments.text: You can see the mistakes.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn si ðə mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: You can correct the movement.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn kərˈɛkt ðə ˈmuvmənt/

segments.text: You can understand the pattern.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˌʌndərˈstænd ðə ˈpætərn/

segments.text: This is true in languages, in music, in everything.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz tru ɪn ˈlæŋɡwədʒəz ɪn ˈmjuzɪk ɪn ˈɛvriˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: If a pianist plays too fast, too early, mistakes become habits.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ə piˈænəst pleɪz tu fæst tu ˈɝli mɪˈsteɪks bɪˈkʌm ˈhæbəts/

segments.text: But if they slow down and if they play slowly and correctly, the fingers will learn the right movement.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ðeɪ sloʊ daʊn ənd ɪf ðeɪ pleɪ ˈsloʊli ənd kərˈɛktli ðə ˈfɪŋɡərz wɪl lɝn ðə raɪt ˈmuvmənt/

segments.text: Later, speed can come.
segments.ipa: /ˈleɪtər spid kæn kʌm/

segments.text: This is also true in English.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ tru ɪn ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: Many learners want to speak fast.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz wɑnt tu spik fæst/

segments.text: They think fast speaking means fluent speaking.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk fæst ˈspikɪŋ minz ˈfluənt ˈspikɪŋ/

segments.text: But if you speak fast with unclear pronunciation, weak grammar, and panic, communication becomes hard.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf ju spik fæst wɪð ənˈklɪr proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən wik ˈɡræmər ənd ˈpænɪk kəmˌjunəˈkeɪʃən bɪˈkʌmz hɑrd/

segments.text: It is better to speak slowly and clearly first.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈbɛtər tu spik ˈsloʊli ənd ˈklɪrli fɝst/

segments.text: Later, your speed will grow naturally.
segments.ipa: /ˈleɪtər jɔr spid wɪl ɡroʊ ˈnætʃərəli/

segments.text: So, slow first, clear first, natural speed later.
segments.ipa: /soʊ sloʊ fɝst klɪr fɝst ˈnætʃərəl spid ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: This is a very important idea.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈvɛri ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: For pronunciation, slow practice is especially useful.
segments.ipa: /fɔr proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən sloʊ ˈpræktəs ɪz əˈspɛʃli ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: Choose one sentence.
segments.ipa: /tʃuz wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Listen to it. Repeat slowly.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən tu ɪt rɪˈpit ˈsloʊli/

segments.text: Notice the sounds.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊtəs ðə saʊndz/

segments.text: Notice which words are stressed.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊtəs wɪtʃ wɝdz ɑr strɛst/

segments.text: Notice where the voice goes up and down.
segments.ipa: /ˈnoʊtəs wɛr ðə vɔɪs ɡoʊz ʌp ənd daʊn/

segments.text: Then, repeat again.
segments.ipa: /ðɛn rɪˈpit əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: Do not rush.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt rʌʃ/

segments.text: Feel each word.
segments.ipa: /fil itʃ wɝd/

segments.text: Say it with rhythm.
segments.ipa: /seɪ ɪt wɪð ˈrɪðəm/

segments.text: Slow practice helps your mouth learn.
segments.ipa: /sloʊ ˈpræktəs hɛlps jɔr maʊθ lɝn/

segments.text: For listening, slowing down is also useful.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈsloʊɪŋ daʊn ɪz ˈɔlsoʊ ˈjusfəl/

segments.text: You can listen to a short part again and again.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈlɪsən tu ə ʃɔrt pɑrt əˈɡɛn ənd əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: You can use slower audio if needed.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn jus ˈsloʊər ˈɑdiˌoʊ ɪf ˈnidəd/

segments.text: You can read the transcript.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn rɛd ðə ˈtrænˌskrɪpt/

segments.text: You can listen again without the transcript.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn wɪˈθaʊt ðə ˈtrænˌskrɪpt/

segments.text: You can focus on one phrase.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˈfoʊkəs ɑn wʌn freɪz/

segments.text: This is much better than listening to one difficult video and understanding almost nothing.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz mʌtʃ ˈbɛtər ðæn ˈlɪsənɪŋ tu wʌn ˈdɪfəkəlt ˈvɪdioʊ ənd ˌʌndərˈstændɪŋ ˈɔlˌmoʊst ˈnʌθɪŋ/

segments.text: Slow learning is not weak learning.
segments.ipa: /sloʊ ˈlɝnɪŋ ɪz nɑt wik ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Slow learning is deep learning.
segments.ipa: /sloʊ ˈlɝnɪŋ ɪz dip ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Many learners feel ashamed when they need slow material.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz fil əˈʃeɪmd wɛn ðeɪ nid sloʊ məˈtɪriəl/

segments.text: They think, "I should understand fast English."
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk aɪ ʃʊd ˌʌndərˈstænd fæst ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ/

segments.text: But, if slow English helps you build the foundation, use it.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ɪf sloʊ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ hɛlps ju bɪld ðə faʊnˈdeɪʃən jus ɪt/

segments.text: There is no shame.
segments.ipa: /ðɛr ɪz noʊ ʃeɪm/

segments.text: A strong foundation makes advanced listening easier later.
segments.ipa: /ə strɔŋ faʊnˈdeɪʃən meɪks ədˈvænst ˈlɪsənɪŋ ˈiziər ˈleɪtər/

segments.text: The practicing mind does not care about looking impressive.
segments.ipa: /ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd dʌz nɑt kɛr əˈbaʊt ˈlʊkɪŋ ˌɪmˈprɛsɪv/

segments.text: It cares about real improvement.
segments.ipa: /ɪt kɛrz əˈbaʊt ril ˌɪmˈpruvmənt/

segments.text: This is a beautiful point.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ə ˈbjutəfəl pɔɪnt/

segments.text: Sometimes we want to practice in a way that makes us feel advanced.
segments.ipa: /səmˈtaɪmz wi wɑnt tu ˈpræktəs ɪn ə weɪ ðæt meɪks ʌs fil ədˈvænst/

segments.text: We choose hard materials.
segments.ipa: /wi tʃuz hɑrd məˈtɪriəlz/

segments.text: We speak too fast.
segments.ipa: /wi spik tu fæst/

segments.text: We avoid basics.
segments.ipa: /wi əˈvɔɪd ˈbeɪsɪks/

segments.text: We want to prove something.
segments.ipa: /wi wɑnt tu pruv ˈsʌmθɪŋ/

segments.text: But practice is not about proving.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈpræktəs ɪz nɑt əˈbaʊt ˈpruvɪŋ/

segments.text: Practice is about improving.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ɪz əˈbaʊt ˌɪmˈpruvɪŋ/

segments.text: If slow practice improves you, slow practice is intelligent.
segments.ipa: /ɪf sloʊ ˈpræktəs ˌɪmˈpruvz ju sloʊ ˈpræktəs ɪz ˌɪnˈtɛlədʒənt/

segments.text: If simple material helps you, simple material is intelligent.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈsɪmpəl məˈtɪriəl hɛlps ju ˈsɪmpəl məˈtɪriəl ɪz ˌɪnˈtɛlədʒənt/

segments.text: If repeating one sentence helps you, repetition is intelligent.
segments.ipa: /ɪf rɪˈpitɪŋ wʌn ˈsɛntəns hɛlps ju ˌrɛpəˈtɪʃən ɪz ˌɪnˈtɛlədʒənt/

segments.text: Do what helps you, not what looks impressive.
segments.ipa: /du wʌt hɛlps ju nɑt wʌt lʊks ˌɪmˈprɛsɪv/

segments.text: Slowing down also helps with stress.
segments.ipa: /ˈsloʊɪŋ daʊn ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps wɪð strɛs/

segments.text: When you rush, your body becomes tense.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju rʌʃ jɔr ˈbɑdi bɪˈkʌmz tɛns/

segments.text: Your breathing becomes short.
segments.ipa: /jɔr ˈbriðɪŋ bɪˈkʌmz ʃɔrt/

segments.text: Your thoughts become noisy.
segments.ipa: /jɔr θɔts bɪˈkʌm ˈnɔɪzi/

segments.text: But when you slow down, your body relaxes.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛn ju sloʊ daʊn jɔr ˈbɑdi rɪˈlæksɪz/

segments.text: You can think more clearly.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn θɪŋk mɔr ˈklɪrli/

segments.text: You can learn more calmly.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn lɝn mɔr ˈkɑmli/

segments.text: For English speaking, try this.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈspikɪŋ traɪ ðɪs/

segments.text: Before answering, pause for 1 second.
segments.ipa: /bɪˈfɔr ˈænsərɪŋ pɔz fɔr ˈsɛkənd/

segments.text: Take a breath. Then, speak.
segments.ipa: /teɪk ə brɛθ ðɛn spik/

segments.text: This short pause can make your answer better.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ʃɔrt pɔz kæn meɪk jɔr ˈænsər ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: It gives your mind time.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɡɪvz jɔr maɪnd taɪm/

segments.text: It makes you sound more thoughtful.
segments.ipa: /ɪt meɪks ju saʊnd mɔr ˈθɔtfəl/

segments.text: It reduces panic.
segments.ipa: /ɪt rəˈdusəz ˈpænɪk/

segments.text: A pause is not failure.
segments.ipa: /ə pɔz ɪz nɑt ˈfeɪljər/

segments.text: A pause is control.
segments.ipa: /ə pɔz ɪz kənˈtroʊl/

segments.text: Many learners are afraid of silence.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈlɝnərz ɑr əˈfreɪd ʌv ˈsaɪləns/

segments.text: They think they must answer immediately.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk ðeɪ mʌst ˈænsər ˌɪˈmiˌdiətli/

segments.text: But even native speakers pause.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈivɪn ˈneɪtɪv ˈspikərz pɔz/

segments.text: Good speakers pause. Teachers pause. Leaders pause.
segments.ipa: /ɡʊd ˈspikərz pɔz ˈtitʃərz pɔz ˈlidərz pɔz/

segments.text: A short pause can make speech stronger.
segments.ipa: /ə ʃɔrt pɔz kæn meɪk spitʃ ˈstrɔŋər/

segments.text: So practice calm pauses.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ˈpræktəs kɑm ˈpɔzəz/

segments.text: If someone asks you a question, you can say "That's a good question.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ˈsʌmˌwʌn æsks ju ə ˈkwɛstʃən ju kæn seɪ ðæts ə ɡʊd ˈkwɛstʃən/

segments.text: Let me think for a second."
segments.ipa: /lɛt mi θɪŋk fɔr ə ˈsɛkənd/

segments.text: Or I would say These phrases give you time.
segments.ipa: /ɔr aɪ wʊd seɪ ðiz ˈfreɪzəz ɡɪv ju taɪm/

segments.text: They help you slow down.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ hɛlp ju sloʊ daʊn/

segments.text: Slowing down also helps you avoid multitasking.
segments.ipa: /ˈsloʊɪŋ daʊn ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps ju əˈvɔɪd ˈmʌltiˌtæskɪŋ/

segments.text: Multitasking means doing many things at the same time.
segments.ipa: /ˈmʌltiˌtæskɪŋ minz ˈduɪŋ ˈmɛni θɪŋz æt ðə seɪm taɪm/

segments.text: Many people listen to English while checking messages, thinking about work, and looking at social media.
segments.ipa: /ˈmɛni ˈpipəl ˈlɪsən tu ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ waɪl ˈtʃɛkɪŋ ˈmɛsədʒəz ˈθɪŋkɪŋ əˈbaʊt wɝk ənd ˈlʊkɪŋ æt ˈsoʊʃəl ˈmidiə/

segments.text: This is not deep practice.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz nɑt dip ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: It may give some exposure, but it is not focused.
segments.ipa: /ɪt meɪ ɡɪv sʌm ɪkˈspoʊʒər bʌt ɪt ɪz nɑt ˈfoʊkəst/

segments.text: For deep practice, choose one thing. Just listen. Just repeat. Just read. Just speak.
segments.ipa: /fɔr dip ˈpræktəs tʃuz wʌn θɪŋ dʒʌst ˈlɪsən dʒʌst rɪˈpit dʒʌst rɛd dʒʌst spik/

segments.text: One task with attention is better than five tasks with no attention.
segments.ipa: /wʌn tæsk wɪð əˈtɛnʃən ɪz ˈbɛtər ðæn faɪv tæsks wɪð noʊ əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: The book teaches that focus grows when we keep bringing the mind back to the task.
segments.ipa: /ðə bʊk ˈtitʃəz ðæt ˈfoʊkəs ɡroʊz wɛn wi kip ˈbrɪŋɪŋ ðə maɪnd bæk tu ðə tæsk/

segments.text: You do not need perfect focus.
segments.ipa: /ju du nɑt nid pərˈfɛkt ˈfoʊkəs/

segments.text: Your mind will move away.
segments.ipa: /jɔr maɪnd wɪl muv əˈweɪ/

segments.text: That is normal.
segments.ipa: /ðæt ɪz ˈnɔrməl/

segments.text: When you notice, bring it back gently.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju ˈnoʊtəs brɪŋ ɪt bæk ˈdʒɛntli/

segments.text: If you're listening, return to the sound.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jʊr ˈlɪsənɪŋ rɪˈtɝn tu ðə saʊnd/

segments.text: If you're reading, return to the sentence.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jʊr ˈridɪŋ rɪˈtɝn tu ðə ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: If you're speaking, return to the idea.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jʊr ˈspikɪŋ rɪˈtɝn tu ðə aɪˈdiə/

segments.text: If you're practicing pronunciation, return to the mouth movement.
segments.ipa: /ɪf jʊr ˈpræktəsɪŋ proʊˌnʌnsiˈeɪʃən rɪˈtɝn tu ðə maʊθ ˈmuvmənt/

segments.text: This is m- mental training.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz ɛm ˈmɛntəl ˈtreɪnɪŋ/

segments.text: Slow practice also helps you enjoy the process.
segments.ipa: /sloʊ ˈpræktəs ˈɔlsoʊ hɛlps ju ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ðə ˈprɑˌsɛs/

segments.text: When you rush, you do not enjoy anything.
segments.ipa: /wɛn ju rʌʃ ju du nɑt ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ ˈɛniˌθɪŋ/

segments.text: You only want to finish.
segments.ipa: /ju ˈoʊnli wɑnt tu ˈfɪnɪʃ/

segments.text: But when you slow down, you can notice small improvements.
segments.ipa: /bʌt wɛn ju sloʊ daʊn ju kæn ˈnoʊtəs smɔl ˌɪmˈpruvmənts/

segments.text: You can enjoy one clear sentence.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ wʌn klɪr ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: You can enjoy one phrase you understand.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ wʌn freɪz ju ˌʌndərˈstænd/

segments.text: You can enjoy one sound that becomes better.
segments.ipa: /ju kæn ˌɛnˈdʒɔɪ wʌn saʊnd ðæt bɪˈkʌmz ˈbɛtər/

segments.text: Joy in practice is important because it helps you continue.
segments.ipa: /dʒɔɪ ɪn ˈpræktəs ɪz ˌɪmˈpɔrtənt bɪˈkɔz ɪt hɛlps ju kənˈtɪnju/

segments.text: For English learners, here is a simple slow practice routine.
segments.ipa: /fɔr ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ˈlɝnərz hir ɪz ə ˈsɪmpəl sloʊ ˈpræktəs ruˈtin/

segments.text: Choose 30 seconds of audio.
segments.ipa: /tʃuz ˈsɛkəndz ʌv ˈɑdiˌoʊ/

segments.text: Listen once for meaning.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən wʌns fɔr ˈminɪŋ/

segments.text: Listen again and notice phrases.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən əˈɡɛn ənd ˈnoʊtəs ˈfreɪzəz/

segments.text: Choose one sentence.
segments.ipa: /tʃuz wʌn ˈsɛntəns/

segments.text: Repeat it slowly five times.
segments.ipa: /rɪˈpit ɪt ˈsloʊli faɪv taɪmz/

segments.text: Record yourself once.
segments.ipa: /rəˈkɔrd jərˈsɛlf wʌns/

segments.text: Listen and choose one small improvement. Repeat again.
segments.ipa: /ˈlɪsən ənd tʃuz wʌn smɔl ˌɪmˈpruvmənt rɪˈpit əˈɡɛn/

segments.text: This is not a long practice, but it is deep.
segments.ipa: /ðɪs ɪz nɑt ə lɔŋ ˈpræktəs bʌt ɪt ɪz dip/

segments.text: It is focused.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈfoʊkəst/

segments.text: It is calm.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz kɑm/

segments.text: It is powerful.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz ˈpaʊərfəl/

segments.text: So, the lesson of this part is simple. Slow down.
segments.ipa: /soʊ ðə ˈlɛsən ʌv ðɪs pɑrt ɪz ˈsɪmpəl sloʊ daʊn/

segments.text: Do not rush your learning.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt rʌʃ jɔr ˈlɝnɪŋ/

segments.text: Do not confuse speed with skill.
segments.ipa: /du nɑt kənfˈjuz spid wɪð skɪl/

segments.text: Practice slowly enough to notice, correct, and understand.
segments.ipa: /ˈpræktəs ˈsloʊli ɪˈnʌf tu ˈnoʊtəs kərˈɛkt ənd ˌʌndərˈstænd/

segments.text: Slow practice builds strong foundations.
segments.ipa: /sloʊ ˈpræktəs bɪldz strɔŋ faʊnˈdeɪʃənz/

segments.text: Strong foundations make future speed possible.
segments.ipa: /strɔŋ faʊnˈdeɪʃənz meɪk ˈfjutʃər spid ˈpɑsəbəl/

segments.text: If you want to go faster later, learn slowly now. All right.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju wɑnt tu ɡoʊ ˈfæstər ˈleɪtər lɝn ˈsloʊli naʊ ɔl raɪt/

segments.text: Now, let's talk about mistakes.
segments.ipa: /naʊ lɛts tɔk əˈbaʊt mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: Mistakes are a normal part of practice.
segments.ipa: /mɪˈsteɪks ɑr ə ˈnɔrməl pɑrt ʌv ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: But many people hate mistakes.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ˈmɛni ˈpipəl heɪt mɪˈsteɪks/

segments.text: They feel embarrassed.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ fil ɪmˈbɛrəst/

segments.text: They feel angry.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ fil ˈæŋɡri/

segments.text: They feel discouraged.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ fil dɪˈskɝədʒd/

segments.text: They think a mistake means they are not good.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk ə mɪˈsteɪk minz ðeɪ ɑr nɑt ɡʊd/

segments.text: They think a mistake means they are failing.
segments.ipa: /ðeɪ θɪŋk ə mɪˈsteɪk minz ðeɪ ɑr ˈfeɪlɪŋ/

segments.text: But the practicing mind teaches us to see mistakes differently.
segments.ipa: /bʌt ðə ˈpræktəsɪŋ maɪnd ˈtitʃəz ʌs tu si mɪˈsteɪks ˈdɪfrəntli/

segments.text: A mistake is not the enemy.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk ɪz nɑt ðə ˈɛnəmi/

segments.text: A mistake is information.
segments.ipa: /ə mɪˈsteɪk ɪz ˌɪnfərˈmeɪʃən/

segments.text: It shows you what needs attention.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ʃoʊz ju wʌt nidz əˈtɛnʃən/

segments.text: It shows you where to practice.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ʃoʊz ju wɛr tu ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: It shows you the next step.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ʃoʊz ju ðə nɛkst stɛp/

segments.text: If you are learning English and you make a grammar mistake, the mistake is not proof that you cannot learn.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju ɑr ˈlɝnɪŋ ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ ənd ju meɪk ə ˈɡræmər mɪˈsteɪk ðə mɪˈsteɪk ɪz nɑt pruf ðæt ju ˈkænɑt lɝn/

segments.text: It is just showing you a pattern that needs more practice.
segments.ipa: /ɪt ɪz dʒʌst ˈʃoʊɪŋ ju ə ˈpætərn ðæt nidz mɔr ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: If you pronounce a word unclearly, the mistake shows you which sound to practice.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju prəˈnaʊns ə wɝd unclearly ðə mɪˈsteɪk ʃoʊz ju wɪtʃ saʊnd tu ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: If you forget a sound while speaking, the mistake shows you that you need to use that word more often.
segments.ipa: /ɪf ju fərˈɡɛt ə saʊnd waɪl ˈspikɪŋ ðə mɪˈsteɪk ʃoʊz ju ðæt ju nid tu jus ðæt wɝd mɔr ˈɔfən/

segments.text: Mistakes guide practice.
segments.ipa: /mɪˈsteɪks ɡaɪd ˈpræktəs/

segments.text: Without mistakes, you would not know what to improve.
segments.ipa: /wɪˈθaʊt mɪˈsteɪks ju wʊd nɑt noʊ wʌt tu ˌɪmˈpruv/
